question: U10's shared-set test: do the 5 and 10 tile lists picked in full (Code, Quote, Accordion; Video, Map) predict other types' lists? Predictions from those picks, pushed before any read. Two picks per type, Blocks Probe, unsaved, one type per reload.
basis: 5 tiles (CAP-U10PICK-CODE, QUOTE, ACCORDION): each pick has a fixed desktop row start and columns, phone row start and columns, rows past the block and look; the block's height is its content's. 10 tiles (CAP-U10PICK-VIDEO, MAP): the same, with no rows past the block. Ours builds the 13 unread 5 and 10 tile lists by this rule now (inferred).

predictions.predict: the same as Code's read picks 1 and 4 exactly, since its tile heights equal Code's to 0.1px: pick 1 desktop 8/15/10/25, phone 2/2/4/10, 9 rows, soft divider; pick 4 desktop 3/10/5/18, phone 1/2/3/10, 6 rows, dark
desktop row start 3, columns 3-13 (end column exclusive: 3/13); phone row start 2, columns 2/10; section rows = desktop end row - 1 + 4; look: dark, rounded divider
desktop row start 3, columns 10-18 (end column exclusive: 10/18); phone row start 1, columns 2/10; section rows = desktop end row - 1 + 2; look: dark

the block's phone height is the same in both picks. Desktop height is not predicted: its content follows its width, and ours keeps the block's own height, so a change with width is a named miss of the rule, not a pass
desktop row start 5, columns 7-21 (end column exclusive: 7/21); phone row start 2, columns 2/10; section rows = desktop end row - 1 + 4; look: none
desktop row start 4, columns 9-19 (end column exclusive: 9/19); phone row start 1, columns 2/10; section rows = desktop end row - 1 + 3; look: none

the block's phone height is the same in both picks. Desktop height is not predicted: its content follows its width, and ours keeps the block's own height, so a change with width is a named miss of the rule, not a pass
desktop 1/7/1+h/21, phone 3/1/3+p/11, section rows = h (no rows past the block), no theme, no divider
desktop 1/1/1+h/14, phone 1/1/1+p/11, section rows = h, no theme, no divider; h is the same as in pick 2, since tiles 1 to 7 are all 45.6px (Zola doesn't follow its width)

predictions.case: Scrolling alone, picks 0 and 2 (6 tiles, no picked partner: a weak guess)
predictions.predict: tiles 0 and 2 are both 111.5px, so: the same section rows, the same block height and the same look in both, and different desktop columns

ifMiss: a type that misses goes back to count and order, its areas named not read (lead, 2026-11-07)
scored: 5 of 10 held (CAP-U10SHARE-MARKDOWN, INSTAGRAM, CHART, ZOLA, SCROLLING). Held: Markdown picks 1 and 4 (exactly Code's); Zola picks 2 and 5 (1/7/3/21 and 1/1/3/14, phone 3/1/5/11 and 1/1/3/11, 2 rows, no style); Instagram's phone height the same in both picks (34 rows); Scrolling's weak guess (10 rows, block 2 rows, no style in both; columns 1/27 and 2/26). Missed: Instagram pick 2 (3/3/22/19, no theme or divider, not 3/3/../13 dark rounded), Instagram pick 4 (2/8/16/20, phone row 2, not 3/10/../18, phone row 1); Chart pick 0 (3/3/21/25, not 5/7/../21), Chart pick 3 (3/9/16/25, dark rounded, not 4/9/../19 with no style), Chart's phone height (21 then 16 rows, not the same). So the 5 tile rule from Code, Quote and Accordion does not hold for Instagram or Chart; the 10 tile rule held for Zola.
